accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Health Education statutory guidance (2019), which lists 'how to make a clear and efficient call to emergency services if necessary' under basic first aid by the end of primary; NHS 'When to call 999' (not breathing, unconscious or not waking, choking, heavy bleeding); fire and rescue advice 'Get out, stay out, call 999'; and Ofcom guidance that 999 and 112 both work in the UK, are free, and can be dialled from a locked phone or one with no credit. The lesson names other countries' numbers (112, 911, 000) so it is not UK-only. It never tells a child they must not call when truly unsure and alone (adult text says calling and explaining is right). Parameterised items checked at the corners: 3n gives 6 to 18 (p2), n-k gives 1 to 5 (p4), nk gives 2 to 15 (m6), n-k gives 3 to 11 minutes (m9).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips adults report for this age: 999 for a graze, a lost tablet or a squabble (each refused on the Help now tray with its own reason), a test or joke call (prediction 1, m5, challenge), ringing 999 instead of fetching a grown-up who is in the garden (scene 2, m1, challenge), staying in a smoky house to call or going back in for toys (prediction 2, the 'Call 999 myself' refusal on the kitchen-fire story, challenge), believing a locked phone or no credit blocks the call (prediction 3, the lock-screen tap refusal, m4), dialling 1 or another digit (keypad refusal), not knowing where you are (the 'I don't know where' chip, m7), talking too fast, and hanging up early (prediction 4, the 'Hang up now' chip, p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagemcall is built on this topic's own mechanics: an emergency or can-wait tray sort, a child token dragged to three decision signs across four stories (fetch the grown-up, call 999 myself, get out then call), a locked phone where only the Emergency button opens the keypad and only 9 9 9 then Call connects, a three-van service picker (ambulance, fire, police), and a call-handler script where each answer only fits its own question. It differs from 1046 flaggetout (escaping a fire), 858 telling a grown-up and 1068 flagleftout; the lab-distinct gate passed against every flag lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is discovered by doing: dropping 'I grazed my knee' on Help now bounces with 'Tell a grown-up and use a plaster'; dragging yourself to 'Get out, then call 999' for the sister's arm gets 'There is no fire here. A grown-up is close by'; tapping the locked keypad says you do not need the passcode and points to Emergency; tapping 1 resets the number with 'In the UK the number is 9 9 9'; dropping 'Gran will not wake up' on Fire gets 'Someone badly hurt or ill needs an Ambulance'; the address chip dropped on 'What has happened?' is sent back to 'Where are you?'. Real mouse drags and taps at 390 px confirmed every one of these messages.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Kai wants to call 999 just to see if it works' (Yes, if he hangs up fast; the Testing 999 card is refused), 'There is smoke in the house. Should you stay inside to call 999?' (Yes, call first; the kitchen-fire story only accepts Get out, then call), 'The phone is locked and has no credit. Can you still call 999?' (No; the Emergency button dials without the code), 'You have said what happened. Can you hang up now?' (Yes, they know now; Hang up now is refused).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions, each wrong answer mapped to its own message: 'Yes, any cut needs 999' gets the graze message, 'Stay in and call 999' gets 'Never stay in a smoky house to call', 'Go back for my toys' gets 'Never go back in for toys or pets', 'Call 999 without telling Mum' gets 'A grown-up is close by. Fetch them fast', 'Nothing, he needs the code' gets the lock-screen message, 'Find someone with credit' gets 'You do not need credit', and 'Say I don't know and stop' gets the street-sign clue. Answer order rotates per question.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday words (hurt, breathe, wake up, fire, danger, call handler) and pass the learner readability limit in learn/validate_lessons.py; adult text passes the adult limit. Canvas labels are two to seven words; each feedback line is one or two short sentences naming what to do instead.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean (no filler phrases). Each kid paragraph carries one part of the routine: what counts as an emergency; grown-up first, or call yourself, fire means get out first; how to dial from a locked phone; what to say and to stay on. Adult paragraphs give the curriculum basis and UK facts, the order of the lab, the common mistakes, and how the lesson differs from the fire-safety and telling-a-grown-up lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 390 px phone screenshots before and after Show me for all five scenes, plus 1200 px desktop in dark theme: eight emergency cards in a 2 x 4 grid over two trays; a story card, the child token and three tall signs (moved up so the tick line under them is clear); a phone frame with lock screen, a large Emergency button, a 3 x 4 keypad and a green Call button; four job cards over three labelled vans; four question rows beside the call handler with seven answer chips in a 2 x 4 grid. Real drags and taps at 390 px worked for card to tray, child to sign, keypad taps, job to van and answer to question.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Help now / Can wait pairs per card with full-sentence aria-labels, one button per decision sign naming the story, Emergency, Dial 9, Dial 1 and Call buttons for the phone, one button per service per problem, and one per answer chip. The canvas aria-label carries the scene instructions, every piece of feedback and the challenge question; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; ticks, crosses and counts mark state as well as colour. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations.
